```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

require(tidyverse)
require(kableExtra)
require(mirt)
require(mirtCAT)
require(ggpubr)
```

When deciding how to assess bilingual children, researcher now have several options, including:
 - full CDI in each language
 - Swadesh-CDI in each language
 - CDI-CATs (for available languages)
 - published short forms (for available languages)
 - DLL-ES (only for English and Spanish)

The question is: what is the best option (or combination), if the goal is to assess children's ability in each language?
We'll start just by looking at a correlation matrix comparing each measure's estimated ability. 

```{r load-data}
# BiLexPo data -- has 'bilingual' identifier in dataset_origin_name
bi_dat <- readRDS("data/bilingual_item_data_clean.Rds") |>
  filter(dataset_origin_name %in% 
           c("Marchman Dallas Bilingual", "Hoff_English_Mexican_Bilingual"))

load("data/new_EN_WS_WG_norms.Rdata") # d_demo, d_mat, d_wide
load("data/wordbank_sp_ws_wg_webcdi12-30mos.Rds") # d_demo, d_mat, d_wide, items
```
